en: Having bowed his head to the god Vināyaka, the son of Gaurī...
One should constantly remember Bhaktāvāsa for the sake of attaining longevity, desire, and success. || 1 ||
First is Vakratuṇḍa, and Ekadanta is the second;
the third is Kṛṣṇapiṅgākṣa, and Gajavaktra is the fourth.
The fifth is Lambodara, and the sixth is Vikaṭa;
the seventh is Vighnarājendra, and the eighth is Dhūmravarṇa.
The ninth is Bhālacandra, the tenth is Vināyaka, the eleventh is Gaṇapati, and the twelfth is Gajānana. || 4 ||
The man who recites these twelve names at the three junctions of the day shall have no fear of obstacles; he is the Lord who grants all accomplishments.
One seeking knowledge obtains knowledge; one seeking wealth obtains wealth;
one seeking a son obtains sons; and one seeking liberation obtains the supreme goal.
One should recite the Gaṇapati-stotra; within six months one shall obtain the fruit, and within a year one attains perfection—of this there is no doubt.
And whoever, having transcribed it, should present it to eight Brahmins,
all knowledge shall belong to him through the grace of Gaṇeśa.
Thus ends the hymn to Gaṇeśa for the destruction of distress in the glorious Nārada Purāṇa.
